intro: Meeting someone after a long time, asking how things are going, sending regards and saying a proper goodbye.
p.cuánto tiempo.consejo: It is an exclamation: «¡cuánto tiempo!». «Cuánto» has an accent because it is exclamatory.
p.me alegro de verte.glosa: I am glad to see you
p.me alegro de verte.consejo: «Alegrarse de» takes an infinitive if the subject is the same: «me alegro de verte».
p.qué tal te va.glosa: how are things going for you?
p.qué tal te va.consejo: It is informal. «Qué tal» has an accent on «qué». You answer with «bien», «tirando» or «fenomenal».
p.tirando.consejo: It comes from «ir tirando». It is what you answer when things are so-so.
p.estupendamente.consejo: It comes from «estupendo» plus «-mente». It is an energetic way of saying «muy bien».
p.cómo va lo de.glosa: how is that business of… going?
p.cómo va lo de.consejo: A noun follows «lo de»: «¿cómo va lo de tu piso?». It shows you remember the subject.
p.dar recuerdos.consejo: It is asked like this: «dale recuerdos a tu madre». «Recuerdos» here are not memories but greetings.
p.de mi parte.consejo: It goes at the end: «dale un abrazo de mi parte». «Parte» is feminine.
p.a ver si nos vemos.glosa: let us see if we can meet up
p.a ver si nos vemos.consejo: It is informal and often closes a goodbye. After «si» comes the indicative: «a ver si nos vemos».
p.lo mismo digo.consejo: You answer a greeting or a wish with it. The d in «digo» is a normal d, not th.
p.pasárselo bien.consejo: It carries «se» and «lo»: «pásatelo bien», «que te lo pases bien». It has an accent on the first a.
p.cruzar los dedos.consejo: People say «crucemos los dedos» to wish for luck. The z in «cruzar» sounds like th.
p.don.consejo: It goes with the first name: «don Ramón». For women it is «doña». It is written in lower case.
p.aprovechar.consejo: It is a very useful verb: «aprovecha estos días». The ch sounds as in «chico».
b1.texto:
**Meeting again.** **¡Hombre, Luis!** **¡Cuánto tiempo!** **Me alegro de verte.** **¿Qué tal te va?**

The answers go beyond «bien»: **Estupendamente.** **Fenomenal.** **Tirando.**

To ask about something specific use **lo de**: **¿Cómo va lo de** tu piso?

**Welcoming.** With the subjunctive: **¡Qué bien que hayas venido!**

**Forms of address.** **Don** and **doña** go with the first name: **don Antonio**, **doña Pilar**. **Señor** and **señora**, with the surname: **el señor García**.

**Regards.** **Dale recuerdos a tu madre de mi parte.** **Dale un abrazo de mi parte.**

**Good wishes.** **Que te lo pases muy bien.** **Aprovecha estos días.** **Crucemos los dedos.** They are returned with **Lo mismo digo.**

**Saying goodbye.** **A ver si nos vemos pronto.** **Hasta la próxima.**
b2.f0.texto: Well, Paco, long time no see!
b2.f1.texto: I am really glad to see you, Teresa.
b2.f3.texto: How are things going for you?
b2.f4.texto: Getting by, with a lot of work.
b2.f5.texto: How is that business of your shop going?
b2.f6.texto: Things are going wonderfully for us.
b2.f7.texto: Give my regards to don Ramón.
b2.f8.texto: Let us see if we can meet up soon.
b4.texto:
Some formulas have a fixed structure:

- **¿Cómo va lo de…?** + noun: **¿cómo va lo de tu piso?**
- **Dale recuerdos a…** and **de mi parte**: **dale recuerdos a tu madre de mi parte**.
- **Que te lo pases bien**: a wish with the subjunctive.
- **Me alegro de que** + subjunctive: **me alegro de que hayas venido**.
- **Aprovecha** estos días: a wish with the imperative.
- **Don** and **doña** go with the first name; **señor** and **señora**, with the surname.
b4.e0.texto: How is that business with your flat going?
b4.e1.texto: Give my regards to your mother.
b4.e2.texto: I am glad you have come.
b5.f0.texto: In the market square, the air smells of ripe fruit and freshly baked bread.
b5.f1.texto: Among the stalls, a woman with a straw hat stops suddenly.
b5.f2.texto: On the other side of the fountain, a tall man raises his hand shyly.
b5.f3.texto: The two recognise each other at once, despite the years.
b5.f4.texto: They hug in the middle of the crowd, among baskets and voices.
b5.f5.texto: They talk about everything at once and interrupt each other with laughter.
b5.f6.texto: She describes her last year as a long race.
b5.f7.texto: He lists his plans on his fingers, one by one.
b5.f8.texto: When the tower clock strikes twelve, the two say goodbye.
b5.f9.texto: He stays still and crosses his fingers behind his back.
b6.o0.refuerzo: It is very positive: it says everything is great.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «ir tirando» is getting by, neither good nor bad.
b6.o2.refuerzo: That answers a wish, not «¿qué tal?».
b6.pregunta: What do you answer if things are neither good nor bad?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: after «qué bien que» comes the perfect subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: It is indicative; this emotion asks for the subjunctive.
b7.o2.refuerzo: It is past indicative; here the subjunctive goes.
b8.frase: A ver si nos vemos pronto
b8.traduccion: Let us see if we can meet up soon
b9.frase: Dale un abrazo a tu hermana de mi ____.
b9.o0.refuerzo: «De mi lado» is not used in this formula.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes: «de mi parte» means «on my behalf».
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «don» goes with the first name.
b10.o1.refuerzo: No: «don» is not used with the surname.
b10.pregunta: Which form of address goes with the first name?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «Have a great time.» (tú)
b12.o0.refuerzo: To ask for silence you put a finger on your lips.
b12.o1.refuerzo: It has nothing to do with counting.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Yes: you cross your fingers so that something goes well.
p.verte.consejo: The v sounds like b. «te» attaches to the infinitive.
p.paja.consejo: Dry stalks used for hats and baskets. The j sounds like h.
p.reconocen.consejo: From «conocer», to know. «reconocer» means to recognise again.
p.enseguida.consejo: Written as one word. It means at once or immediately.
p.cestas.consejo: Woven containers for carrying food. Plural of «cesta».
p.interrumpen.consejo: «interrumpir» means to cut in while someone speaks.
p.enumera.consejo: «enumerar» means to list things one by one. Here it means count.
p.torre.consejo: A tall, narrow building. The double r sounds strong.
p.despiden.consejo: From «despedirse», to say goodbye. The -en ending means they.
p.desear.consejo: «desear buena suerte» means to wish someone good luck.
